slides.title: Your lab doesn't need to match production. It needs to match its *failure modes*.
The digital twin
slides.body:
Same platforms. Same topology. Faithful at scale.
A year later, it proves the *happy path* works.

slides.title: The happy path was never the question
slides.body:
Outages don't come from the topology.
They come from the *seams*.

slides.title: The seams
slides.body:
Failover that breaks only under asymmetric return traffic.
An upgrade that fails on *state left behind*.
A “multicast problem” that was an app design flaw.

slides.title: A replica of a healthy network is healthy
slides.body:
That's the design goal.
It reproduces *none* of it.

slides.title: Write a different spec
slides.body:
Can this lab reproduce
our *last three outages*?

slides.title: Not port count. Not part numbers.
slides.body:
Break the link, watch convergence take the documented path.
Leave stale state behind, run the upgrade again.
Half-apply a change, rehearse the *rollback*.

slides.title: Two switches and a VM
slides.body: …that reproduce last quarter's incident teach more than a rack that mirrors the DC and has *never been broken on purpose*.

slides.title: Only one of them gets tested at 2am.
slides.body:
A lab that matches production proves your design.
A lab that matches its failures proves your *operations*.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
